text_en: Last month I travelled on my own for the first time. I had been thinking of going to Kyoto, but the hotels were expensive, so I went to Nara. Nara is quiet and has deer, and it was great fun. When I couldn't find my way at the station, a stranger kindly showed me. I had thought travelling alone would be lonely, but it wasn't. Next time I'd like to try going to Hokkaido.

text_ja: {市|し}の{図書館|としょかん}を{使|つか}う{皆|みな}さんへのお{知|し}らせです。{本|ほん}は{一人|ひとり}{十冊|じゅっさつ}まで{借|か}りられます。{借|か}りた{本|ほん}は{二週間|にしゅうかん}{以内|いない}に{返|かえ}さなければなりません。{館内|かんない}で{水|みず}やお{茶|ちゃ}を{飲|の}んでもいいですが、{食|た}べ{物|もの}を{食|た}べてはいけません。{本|ほん}を{返|かえ}す{時|とき}は、カウンターに{来|こ}なくてもいいです。{入|い}り{口|ぐち}の{返却|へんきゃく}ポストに{入|い}れてください。
text_en: This is a notice for everyone who uses the city library. Each person can borrow up to ten books. Borrowed books must be returned within two weeks. You may drink water or tea in the building, but you must not eat food. When returning books, you don't need to come to the counter. Please put them in the return box at the entrance.

title_ja: {雨|あめ}の{日曜日|にちようび}
text_ja: {日曜日|にちようび}は、{友達|ともだち}と{公園|こうえん}でテニスをするつもりでした。{朝|あさ}、{空|そら}を{見|み}ると、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}りそうでした。{天気|てんき}{予報|よほう}は「{晴|は}れ」だったのに、{昼|ひる}から{本当|ほんとう}に{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ってきました。それで、テニスはやめて、{友達|ともだち}の{家|いえ}で{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ながらピザを{食|た}べました。とても{楽|たの}しかったので、{雨|あめ}でもよかったと{思|おも}いました。{来週|らいしゅう}{晴|は}れたら、もう{一度|いちど}テニスをしようと{話|はな}しました。
text_en: On Sunday I was planning to play tennis in the park with a friend. In the morning I looked at the sky and it looked like rain. The forecast had said sunny, but from midday it really did start raining. So we gave up on tennis and ate pizza while watching a movie at my friend's place. It was so much fun that I thought the rain was fine after all. We said that if it's sunny next week, we'll try tennis again.

{映画館|えいがかん}に{行|い}った

text_en: Since last week I've had a part-time job at the bakery in front of the station. I work three times a week while studying at university. The manager is kind and the bread is good; it's a great shop. At first I didn't know how to use the register, so a senior co-worker showed me. The manager said, 'If you practise a little every day, you'll soon get good at it.' Now I can use the register on my own.
